messages.subject: pseudo-replicates as visits in pcount()
parts:
Dear unmarked list,

 

I have a dataset of carabid beetle collected in farmland using pitfall traps. The sampling design consists of 80 random sites with (up to) 4 traps each. The 4 traps are located very close together (in the corners of a square with 50cm long edges) so ecologically they can still be regarded as being in the same spot. There was only one catching period (2 weeks). Not all of the traps survived the sampling period, thus some of the sites have data from 3 or less traps.

I wonder if these pseudo-replicates (traps) can be treated as "visits" in pcount() model? I understand that these are not true replicates in time and those beetles that fall into one trap are not "available for catching" in the other traps thus resulting in lower lambda estimate. However, I am mainly interested in differences among sites and impact of site covariates and not so much in the true abundance or detection probability per se. Do you see any other problems with using the pcount() and treating the traps as visits? Any suggestions?

 

thanks in advance

best wishes

Ainars

 

 

Ainars Aunins

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] pseudo-replicates as visits in pcount()
parts:
Dear Ainars,
 I would not recommend this approach because it necessarily violates all of the core assumptions of the binomial N-mixture model and thus the interpretation of things is highly suspect.
 We discuss this a little bit in the new book (Kery and Royle "Applied Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology", see section 6.14, especially the last paragraph, and see also the relevant bits in chapter 10).
 To decide yourself if this is a good approach for your problem you should definite do a simulation study (see chapter 4).
 
 I really encourage you to do the simulation study and, if you do, please report the results back on the unmarked list so that we can all learn from it.
 
regards
andy

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] pseudo-replicates as visits in pcount()
parts:
Dear Ainars,

 

Your idea is one that comes up repeatedly: why not use spatial replicates for N-mixture-model-type abundance estimation in a similar way as spatial replicates are often used instead of temporal replicates in occupancy models ?

 

However, in general I think that this cannot be done: normally, the “closure” assumption will not be met in such cases, because spatial replicate locations will have a different abundance. Interestingly, in your case where the traps are so close one could make the closure assumption if it were not for the fact that the individuals are removed from the population, which again changes N and hence represents a violation of closure.

 

Had your traps been “strung out” in time over a short period of closure, you could use a multinomial N-mixture model with removal design, but due to simultaneous trap deployment, you can’t do this either.

 

So I think you’re limited to modeling relative abundance using some sort of Poisson GLMM.

 

Best regards  -- Marc
